_comment: Print-area dimensions, with provenance per placement.
scripts/store/build_print_files.mjs reads this and refuses to emit a raster
for any placement whose `verified` is false. That is the whole point of the
file: a print file is a physical commitment, and 'this is probably the
standard size' is exactly the reasoning that prints a mug design at cap
dimensions. A number here without a source is a guess wearing a schema.
`source` must name where the number came from. The only source that sets
verified true is a live read of Printful's mockup-generator printfiles
endpoint via lib/store/printful.ts getPrintAreas — the canary's
print-areas step. Nothing else counts, including Printful's own published
help pages, because those describe a product family and not the specific
catalog id we will actually order.

tee.source: recorded in the ufc-store-v1 catalog comments as live-verified on 2026-09-07, but not re-read since and not reproducible from this branch; treat as unconfirmed until the canary runs

hoodie.source: recorded in the ufc-store-v1 catalog comments as 'verified live' on 2026-09-07; the square aspect is the load-bearing claim and it is why the hoodie has its own print file rather than sharing the tee's, but it has not been re-read from this branch

mug.source: unknown. No dimension has ever been read for a mug blank from this codebase. Deliberately null rather than filled with Printful's commonly-quoted 11oz wrap, so the builder fails instead of producing a plausible wrong file.
